text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Elevated 5xx and TLS handshake failures observed for public API (redwood-api). Alert CF-EDGE-502 triggered 2026-03-15T09:20:34Z. Automated checks show spike across eu-west and us-east edges.

bob: I'm oncall — looking at error logs now. Seeing a huge jump in 502/524 and some curl TLS failures from synthetic probes.

carol-eng: Confirm. Quick local check:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.ai/health
*   Trying 104.17.XX.XX...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (104.17.XX.XX) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS handshake error: SSL: certificate verify failed
* curl: (35) SSL: certificate verify failed
```
This looks like TLS handshake failures rather than origin application errors.

dan-netops: Dig and resolver tests show intermittent SERVFAILs for api.redwood.ai from multiple public resolvers. Example: 
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +short
; (no output) -> then SERVFAIL intermittently
```

alice: @cloudflare-status-bot please confirm if there's a Cloudflare edge issue. Also we need scope on customer impact.

cloudflare-status-bot: Cloudflare status: Investigating — some POPs are experiencing degraded TLS termination and routing issues affecting edge-to-origin handshakes. https://status.cloudflare.com/incidents/xxxx (updated 09:23 UTC)

eva-support: Support intake: 12 distinct customer reports in last 10m. Affected: hosted API customers and some Dedicated customers behind CF. Severity: P2 for Hosted API broadly, P1 for 2 Dedicated customers in eu-west currently experiencing hard errors. Customer comms thread created.

bob: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Bypass Cloudflare for affected regions by switching DNS A records to origin IPs (direct origin) OR 2) Try Cloudflare configuration toggles (disable HTTP/2 / force TLS1.2) at edge if Cloudflare recommends. Bypass is fastest but we need to ensure origin accepts direct TLS hostnames and IP allowlist. I prefer bypass for quick customer relief.

alice: Approve bypass. Ensure we lower TTL and notify infra. Also track any rate differences.

carol-eng: Preparing DNS change. Plan: lower TTL to 60, switch A records for api.redwood.ai -> origin IPs (origin nodes behind load balancer). I'll run console update and monitor.

carol-eng: Executing now (09:27 UTC).

bob: Rolling config on origin to accept direct TLS (confirming cert SAN includes api.redwood.ai). Quick nginx check: cert OK. Pushing temporary nginx reload to accept TLSv1.2 only to maximize handshake success:
```
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; # will try to prefer 1.2
```

dan-netops: Also adding temporary firewall rule to allow Cloudflare bypass IPs to origin LB. Watch for client IP preservation.

bob: DNS swap complete at 09:28:10 UTC. Monitoring metrics.

ops-note (bob): Initial metrics after swap: 5xx rate dropped from ~42% -> ~9% in 3m. Latency stable. Still seeing a few TLS failures from a small subset of customers (likely cached routes).

eva-support: Posting status page update and customer message: "We’re currently mitigating an issue impacting API reachability in some regions. Traffic has been temporarily routed directly to our origins to restore service while Cloudflare investigates. We will post updates every 30 minutes." :speech_balloon:

cloudflare-status-bot: Update 09:35 UTC — Cloudflare identified a misconfiguration in a subset of POPs causing TLS handshakes to fail for some TLS profiles. Mitigation rolling; some POPs restored.

alice: Good. Plan for next steps: 1) Keep bypass in place for 30 minutes post-mitigation to ensure stability 2) Revert DNS back to Cloudflare after they confirm global fix and monitor for handshake errors 3) Post-incident RCA with Cloudflare and request credit.

dan-netops: Noted: capture pcap from origin LB for the interval 09:20-09:40 UTC and save to S3 bucket s3://redwood-incident-dumps/cf-2026-03-15.pcap for RCA.

bob: Handing off to alice at 09:40 UTC for followup and postmortem. I'll stay reachable for 30m for rollback if needed.

alice: Taking over. Current status: traffic routed direct, error rates ~<5%, Cloudflare reports partial mitigation. Next update scheduled 10:00 UTC. Action items assigned for RCA, customer comms, and runbook updates.

cloudflare-status-bot: 09:52 UTC — Incident resolved. TLS termination and routing fully recovered across all POPs. Customers may see intermittent issues for a short period as caches propagate.

alice: We will revert DNS back to Cloudflare in 5m once we confirm metrics.

bob: Reverting DNS at 09:56 UTC.

carol-eng: Revert complete at 09:57:48 UTC. Monitoring: no handshake errors seen in the last 10m, 5xx rate steady at baseline.

eva-support: Sent final customer update and marked affected tickets for follow-up.

alice: Incident closed at 10:02 UTC. Postmortem owners: alice (lead), dan-netops (network analysis), carol-eng (deploy/dns timeline), bob (mitigation timeline), eva-support (customer impact). Follow-ups: request Cloudflare RCA and credit, update our incident runbook to include Cloudflare TLS POP degradation steps (bypass DNS, origin TLS fallback), and add automated detection for TLS handshake anomalies in edge metrics.

bob: Thanks team. Small wins: quick bypass + origin TLS fallback minimized customer downtime. Need to formalize the low-TTL DNS flip procedure in runbook. :thumbsup:
